review.title: Typo Gives It Away
review.headline: Farm eggsecuted itself twice, then a Floofer's slip handed Drew the win.
review.summary: Rounds 1 and 2 were muddy. Players argued over how the Owl egg works, and Farm eggsecuted its own Blair, then its own Drew. Meowfia won both rounds with little effort. In round 3 Ellis, a Meowfia Floofer, said "Farm", then admitted Floofer, and the table piled on. Drew banked 14 points in that throw and finished first with 20.

rounds.recap: Players argued over Owl, Pigeon and Eagle egg counts, and Blair's Owl claim was read as broken. Most of the table threw at Blair, who was Farm. Finley, the lone Meowfia Sphinx, won 5 points and took the lead.

Blair, a Floofer, hugged Finley and stayed quiet. Drew's +3 eggs and confused Kookaburra report left the table lost. Drew's report named Ellis as Floofer, but he had said it was unreliable, so nobody used it. Four players threw at Drew, a Farm player, and Meowfia won.
Ellis, a Meowfia Floofer, typed "Farm" and then admitted Floofer. Everyone but Alex, the Mouser, converged on Ellis. Farm won, and Drew's two 7s banked 14 points to put him first.

highlights.text: Ellis claimed Floofer while saying Farm, then called it a typo. The whole table threw at him.
Drew's confused Kookaburra report truthfully named Ellis as Floofer, but the confusion warning made it unusable.
Meowfia Finley claimed Pigeon and nudged suspicion onto Ellis's count. Farm threw at Blair, so Meowfia won without needing a plan.
Alex held an unused Wink. He threw at Casey rather than Ellis, which kept his cover.

confusions.what: Said the Owl egg goes to the Owl's own nest, and used that to accuse Blair.
Said the Owl's egg only goes in its own nest, and claimed Hawk 'gained nothing' while also reporting +1 from Blair.
Said no change to his nest meant 'no one lands on me with a visit that gains eggs', and muddled the visit explanation.
First said his +2 came from visitors to him, then corrected it to the Eagle rule.
Insisted Owl 'their nest' means the Owl's own nest, so Ellis's egg gave him nothing.
Said Owl eggs go to the Owl only when unvisited, and treated Blair's Owl-then-Hawk as a contradiction though roles are re-dealt.
Said the Floofer only blocks visitors to itself, so a hug on Finley would not stop his Hawk. He was hugged.
Called Farm a 'typo' for his own alignment while claiming a cat. He did not know or track that Floofer is a Meowfia-only role.
Claimed Falcon as 'Meowfia-aligned' in his private notes, though he was Farm that round.

worked: The Floofer hug in round 2 let Blair quietly neutralize Finley, the leader, with no visible trace.
Confused reports (Drew in round 2, Casey in round 3) created real doubt about true information.
The throw mechanic in round 3: Drew's two 7s banked 14 points, so a big winning throw mattered for the final standings.
Meowfia not knowing each other: Alex held back and threw at Casey instead of Ellis, which kept him hidden.
problems: The Owl text ('lay an egg in their nest') was read two opposite ways for two rounds. Fix: say 'in the visited player's nest' or 'in your own nest'.
Rule arguments crowded out deduction. Most of the day went on what the rules say, not who lied. Fix: add a short rules recap or card text on each player's screen.
Rounds 1 and 2 had a lone Meowfia and almost no usable evidence, so Farm threw at the loudest accusation. The odds of 1 Meowfia seem too hard on Farm.
The Wink on the Mouser was never used, and Mouser's role info was minor. Consider making the Wink prompt louder or the Mouser more useful.
Speech turns were repetitive: players restated claims and asked 'who visited me?' repeatedly. Fewer beats or a tighter cap would cut the filler.
